## Oral history research {.smaller .scrollable}

Recorded interviews: audio, video, transcripts and the consent that goes with them

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Record and edit audio**

- [Audacity](https://www.audacityteam.org): free audio editor to trim, clean and convert recordings

**Transcribe**

- [noScribe](https://github.com/kaixxx/noScribe): free automatic transcription that runs on your own computer (based on Whisper), so recordings never leave your machine
- [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper): open-source speech recognition in many languages (more technical)
- [oTranscribe](https://otranscribe.com): free browser tool for manual transcription with playback controls
- [ELAN](https://archive.mpi.nl/tla/elan): time-aligned annotation of audio and video

**Index and publish**

- [OHMS](https://www.oralhistoryonline.org): link transcripts and keyword indexes to points in the recording
- [Aviary](https://www.aviaryplatform.com): host searchable audio and video collections
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Analyse (code themes in interviews)**

- [QualCoder](https://qualcoder.wordpress.com) and [Taguette](https://www.taguette.org): free qualitative coding tools
- [NVivo](https://lumivero.com/products/nvivo/), [MAXQDA](https://www.maxqda.com), [ATLAS.ti](https://atlasti.com): commercial tools, often licensed by institutions

**Archive and share**

- [QDR – Qualitative Data Repository](https://qdr.syr.edu), [UK Data Service](https://ukdataservice.ac.uk), or an institutional repository, with access restrictions where needed

**Ethics and good practice**

- [Oral History Association principles](https://oralhistory.org/principles-and-best-practices-revised-2018/) and [Oral History Society](https://www.ohs.org.uk) guidance
- Plan informed consent, GDPR compliance and anonymisation *before* recording

::: {.callout-warning}
## Check before you upload
Interviews contain personal data. Ask your data protection office before sending recordings to an online transcription service.
:::
